_comment: Night-run expansion, 2026-10-01 (profile 'full' only; the 57-Item base seed in items.json stays the regression set). Same authoring conventions as items.json. Every date was read in the cited English Wikipedia revision (index: wikipedia_evidence.json); labels keep the source wording. Coordinates, countries, admin areas, Hebrew labels and Wikidata dates come from the Wikidata snapshot. Unknowns are left unknown.

items.name: Obelisk of Aksum
items.description: 4th-century CE phonolite stele at Aksum; taken to Rome in 1937, returned in 2005, re-erected in 2008.

function.note: Source describes the Aksumite practice of erecting burial steles; function of this stele inferred from that practice.

time.label: probably carved and erected during the 4th century CE
taken to Italy as war spoil (1937)
returned to Ethiopia in three pieces, 19–25 April 2005
re-erected and unveiled 4 September 2008

items.name: Lucy (AL 288-1)
items.description: Partial skeleton of an Australopithecus afarensis individual found at Hadar, Ethiopia.

culture.note: Species, not a culture: POC shortcut (see SPEC_INPUTS.md).

links.note: 'preserved at the National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa'.

time.label: lived around 3.2 million years ago
discovered in 1974 at Hadar
exhibited on a six-year US tour from 2007; original fossils returned to Ethiopia in 2013

items.name: Nebra sky disc
items.description: Bronze disc with gold inlays depicting celestial bodies, found near Nebra (Germany); its dating has been challenged.

function.note: Source: presents solstice knowledge 'in the form of a portable object'.

attrs.value: Gebhard & Krause (2020) proposed an Iron Age date; Pernicka et al. (2020) rejected their arguments.
attrs.note: No numeric alternative range is given in the source, so the challenge is recorded as an attribute claim, not as a time extent.

time.label: dated by archaeologists to c. 1800–1600 BC (Early Bronze Age)
burial: birch bark in the sword hilts radiocarbon-dated to 1600–1560 BCE

time.method: typology of the associated axes and swords
time.label: associated axes and swords dated typologically to c. 1700–1500 BCE
found in 1999 by metal-detecting treasure hunters

items.name: Taputapuātea marae
items.description: Large marae complex on Ra'iātea (Society Islands).

time.label: may have been established as early as AD 1000; abandoned shortly after missionaries arrived in the early 19th century
time.note: 'As early as AD 1000' is a lower bound only; the end bounds are a POC reading of 'early 19th century … shortly thereafter'.

time.label: expanded and rebuilt at least twice between the 14th and 18th centuries
archaeological remains restored in 1994

items.name: Laetoli footprints
items.description: Site in Tanzania with hominin footprints preserved in volcanic ash.

culture.note: 'Australopithecus afarensis is the species most commonly proposed'; tracemaker identity 'much debated'.

time.label: footprints dated to 3.7 million years ago
upper unit of the Laetolil Beds: 3.6 to 3.8 million years ago
tracks discovered by Mary Leakey's team in 1976, excavated by 1978

items.name: Murujuga (Burrup Peninsula) rock-art landscape
items.description: Cultural landscape with one of the world's largest concentrations of petroglyphs. NOTE: the Wikidata item is the Burrup Peninsula (a landform), not a separate 'cultural landscape' entity.

time.label: some carvings dated to more than 45,000 years old
time.note: Only an upper bound on the start is known ('more than'); creation continued over a very long period (not dated in the source).

time.label: some of the collection generally estimated to be 40,000–50,000 years old

items.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
items.description: Mud-brick mosque in Djenné (Mali); the present building dates from 1907, on the site of a mosque first built around the 13th century.

time.label: current structure: rebuilding arranged in 1906, completed in 1907
first mosque on the site: dates as early as 1200 and as late as 1330 have been suggested
time.note: Same Item across rebuilds is a modelling choice (see SPEC_INPUTS.md).

items.name: Cave of Altamira
items.description: Cave in Cantabria with Upper Palaeolithic paintings.

time.label: earliest paintings applied around 36,000 years ago
Upper Solutrean deposits (c. 18,500 years ago)
Lower Magdalenian deposits (c. 16,590–14,000 years ago)
discovered in 1868 by Modesto Cubillas

items.name: Monte Verde
items.description: Late Pleistocene site in southern Chile, central to the debate on the peopling of the Americas.

attrs.value: other researchers suggested MV-II cannot be older than the middle Holocene
attrs.note: No numeric bounds given in the source for this view.

time.label: Monte Verde II: generally suggested to date to 14,500 years ago
time.note: 'Largely accepted (though not without dissent)'.

time.label: average age of 14,800 BP (1982)
time.note: Stated as BP; the source does not say whether calibrated.

time.label: Monte Verde I re-dated (2015) to around 18,500 to 14,500 BP
time.note: MV-I 'lacks the general acceptance of Monte Verde II'.

items.name: Kuk Swamp
items.description: Site in the New Guinea Highlands with evidence of independently developed early agriculture.

time.label: agricultural drainage systems beginning about 9,000 years ago
time.note: Start only; end of use not dated in the source.

time.label: cultivation of bananas and sugar cane, 6,900–6,400 years ago
banana phytoliths indicating deliberate planting, 6950–6550 years ago

items.name: Pueblo Bonito
items.description: Largest Chacoan great house in Chaco Canyon, New Mexico.

time.label: planned and constructed in stages between AD 850 and AD 1150
excavations by Wetherill and Pepper, 1896–1900

items.name: Serpent Mound
items.description: Prehistoric effigy mound in Ohio; who built it, and when, has long been disputed.

culture.note: 2014 radiocarbon (corroborated 2019): built c. 300 BCE by Adena peoples.
1991 charcoal dates c. 1070 CE; rebuilt or repaired c. 1100 CE in the Fort Ancient period.

time.label: built in 300 BCE by the Adena peoples (2014 radiocarbon, corroborated 2019)
time.note: Critique (Lepper): dated material was organic sediment from soil cores, not charcoal from an exposed profile.

time.label: two charcoal samples dated ca. 1070 CE (1991)
rebuilt or repaired around 1100 CE during the Fort Ancient period

items.name: Siloam inscription
items.description: Hebrew inscription recording the construction of the Siloam tunnel; held in Istanbul.

names.name: כתובת השילוח
names.note: Hebrew name supplied by the curator (Claude); not sourced. Wikidata Hebrew label, if any, is imported separately.

links.note: Part of the collections of the Istanbul Archaeology Museum; return requests (2007, 2017) were not granted.

time.label: tunnel and inscription dated to the 8th century BC on the basis of the writing style
found in 1880

items.name: Mesha Stele
items.description: Moabite royal inscription of King Mesha (Moabite Stone).

attrs.value: monarch referred to by three consonants beginning with 'B'; most probably Balak, not David (Finkelstein, Na'aman & Römer 2019)

time.label: dated around 840 BCE
may be as late as 810 BCE (Lemaire)

items.name: Tel Dan stele
items.description: Fragmentary Old Aramaic victory inscription found at Tel Dan; mentions the 'House of David'.

links.note: 'Currently, it is on display at the Israel Museum.'
Most scholars identify Hazael of Damascus (c. 842–806 BCE) as the author.
George Athas: Ben-Hadad III, dating the inscription to around 796 BCE.
Jan-Wim Wesselius: Jehu of Israel (r. c. 845–818 BCE).

time.label: generally dated to the 9th century BCE
earliest possible c. 870 BCE; latest 'hardly much later than 750' (Mykytiuk)
around 796 BCE if by Ben-Hadad III (Athas)
fragment A found 1993; fragments B1 and B2 in June 1994

items.name: Aleppo Codex
items.description: 10th-century manuscript of the Hebrew Bible written in Tiberias; damaged in 1947, partly lost.

names.name: כתר ארם צובא
names.note: Hebrew name as given in the source (Keter Aram-Tsova, 'Crown of Aleppo').

links.note: Surviving portion housed in the Shrine of the Book at the Israel Museum.

attrs.value: roughly 40% missing when it resurfaced in 1958, including most of the Torah

time.label: written in Tiberias in the 10th century CE (circa 920)
synagogue of Aleppo torched during anti-Jewish riots in 1947
resurfaced in Israel in 1958

items.name: Tel Megiddo
items.description: Tell of ancient Megiddo in the Jezreel Valley.

time.label: occupied continuously from the early Bronze Age (c. 3000 BCE) to the Persian period (c. 332 BCE)
inhabited approximately from 5000 to 350 BCE
or even since around 7000 BCE (Megiddo Expedition suggestion)
time.note: Start only.

time.label: Early Bronze IB temple: calibrated dates from the 31st and 30th century BCE

items.name: Chicxulub crater
items.description: Buried impact crater under the Yucatán Peninsula, linked to the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary.

time.label: formed slightly over 66 million years ago
time.note: 'Slightly over' = an upper bound on the date (it happened at or before 66 Ma).

time.label: magnetic survey 1978; identification published 1991

items.name: Buddhas of Bamiyan
items.description: Two monumental Buddhist reliefs in the Bamiyan Valley, destroyed in March 2001.

time.label: smaller 'Eastern Buddha' built around 570 CE
larger 'Western Buddha' built around 618 CE
carved around 600 CE during Hephthalite rule
destroyed in March 2001

items.name: Kilwa Kisiwani
items.description: Island ruins of the medieval Swahili city-state of Kilwa.

time.label: founding confirmed at the start of the 9th century CE
time.note: Start only; the island is still inhabited.

time.label: highest point in wealth and commerce between the 13th and 15th centuries

items.name: Sanchi Stupa
items.description: Buddhist complex in Madhya Pradesh centred on the Great Stupa.

links.note: 'originally commissioned by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE'.

time.label: originally commissioned in the 3rd century BCE
four carved toranas and a balustrade added in the 1st century BCE
the complex flourished until the 11th century

items.name: Yinxu
items.description: Ruins of Yin, last capital of the Shang dynasty, near Anyang; source of oracle-bone inscriptions.

time.label: capital during the Late Shang period (c. 1250 – c. 1046 BCE)
rediscovered in 1899 through oracle bones sold nearby

items.name: Hattusa
items.description: Capital of the Hittite Empire in central Anatolia.

time.label: earliest traces of settlement from the 6th millennium BC
burned and ruined around 1700 BC (attributed to Anitta of Kussara)
Hittite capital from around 1650 BC (Labarna/Hattusili)
time.note: End of the capital phase not captured from the source extract.

items.name: Troy (Hisarlık)
items.description: Bronze Age city in north-west Anatolia, generally identified with Homer's Troy and Hittite Wilusa.

attrs.value: Hisarlık is generally identified with Hittite Wilusa/Truwisa and with Homeric Troy

time.label: first settled around 3600 BC; '4000 years of settlement'
time.note: End of settlement not captured (open).

time.label: grew into a small fortified city around 3000 BC (Troy I)

items.name: Babylon
items.description: Capital of Babylonia on the Euphrates.

names.name: בבל
names.note: Hebrew name supplied by the curator (Claude); not sourced.

time.label: earliest known mention on a tablet from the reign of Shar-Kali-Sharri (2217–2193 BC)
from the earliest mention to the last known habitation (11th century AD)
capital of the Neo-Babylonian Empire, 626–539 BC

items.name: Palmyra
items.description: Ancient caravan city in the Syrian Desert; large parts destroyed in 2015.

time.label: documents first mention the city in the early second millennium BCE
time.note: Numeric bounds are a POC reading of 'early second millennium BCE'.

time.label: by the third century, a prosperous regional center
captured in 2015 by the Islamic State, which destroyed large parts of the ancient city

items.name: Harappa
items.description: Major city of the Indus Valley Civilisation in Punjab.

time.label: Mature Harappan phase (2600 BC – 1900 BC), the city's greatest extent
the civilization's mature phase lasted from 2600 BC to 2000 BC
time.note: Same article gives two end dates for the mature phase.

time.label: bricks taken for railway ballast in 1857

items.name: Ajanta Caves
items.description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in Maharashtra.

time.label: first phase: 2nd century BCE to 1st century CE
first phase 100 BCE – 100 CE (Walter Spink)
second phase 400–650 CE according to older accounts
second phase in a brief period of 460–480 CE according to later scholarship
'discovered' in 1819 by Colonel John Smith

items.name: Bagan
items.description: Capital of the Pagan Kingdom with thousands of Buddhist temples.

time.label: capital of the Pagan Kingdom from the 9th to 13th centuries
more than 10,000 religious buildings constructed between the 11th and 13th centuries
founded in the mid-to-late 9th century (Western scholarship)
time.note: The Burmese chronicles give a different (earlier) founding; their date was not captured from the source extract.

items.name: Chauvet Cave
items.description: Cave in the Ardèche with some of the oldest known figurative cave paintings; dating has been disputed.

time.label: art placed in the Aurignacian, approximately 32,000–30,000 years ago (2012 study)
first period of habitation 37,000–33,500 years ago, when most black drawings were made (2016 study)
second period of habitation 31,000–28,000 years ago (2016 study)
later Gravettian occupation 27,000–25,000 years ago

items.name: Ötzi
items.description: Natural mummy of a man who lived in the 4th millennium BC, found in the Ötztal Alps.

located_in.note: Found at the Austria–Italy border; the source says it was initially unclear on which side.

time.label: lived between 3359 and 3105 BC
death: 66% probability between 3239 and 3105 BC
death: 33% probability between 3359 and 3294 BC
discovered on 19 September 1991

items.name: Hadrian's Wall
items.description: Roman frontier fortification across northern Britain.

time.label: begun in AD 122 in the reign of Hadrian
time.note: Completion date not captured from the source extract.

time.label: Roman frontier until the end of Roman rule in Britain in 410 AD

items.name: Hagia Sophia
items.description: Justinian's basilica in Istanbul: church, mosque, museum and mosque again — function changes over time.

function.note: Mosque after the fall of Constantinople in 1453 (until 1934/35) and again since 2020 — two periods on one claim; see SPEC_INPUTS.md (time-scoped relations).

time.label: current structure built by Justinian I between 532 and 537
earlier 'Great Church' constructed by Constantius c. 346 (Socrates of Constantinople)
time.note: Ancient report; whether that church was already called Hagia Sophia is questioned (Mainstone).

time.label: became a mosque after the fall of Constantinople (1453)
opened as a museum in 1935
reclassified as a mosque in 2020

Paracas phase, 400 to 200 BC
Nazca phase, 200 BC to 500 AD
